summary: Anthropic's 15 April 2026 major outage affected Claude.ai, the API and Claude Code for about two hours and forty-nine minutes, with problems continuing after an initial fix announcement. Reporters observed failed login and verification flows, an unused free account falsely shown as having exhausted its prompt allowance, service-busy errors, a Pro upgrade suggestion and model-unavailable messages that did not provide a working recovery path. Login began working again before prompts reliably returned responses. Anthropic reported API recovery separately and marked the full incident resolved at 1:42 PM ET.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Anthropic acknowledged elevated errors on Claude.ai, the API and Claude Code at 10:53 AM ET on 15 April 2026, said an initial fix was being implemented, later reported Claude.ai and Platform down with Claude Code login unavailable through Claude.ai, and marked the incident resolved at 1:42 PM ET. TechRadar reporters observed failed mobile login, failed Pro verification-code submission, an unused free account shown as prompt-limit exhausted, service-busy errors, a Pro upgrade suggestion and a model-unavailable message whose suggested switch did not restore responses. The recovered original status page distinguishes API recovery and use by already logged-in Code users from continuing new-login failure. Its API-recovery update contains conflicting clock times, so exact API recovery ordering is not established. The first 15:03 UTC update announces fix implementation, not completed recovery.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The material failure was the conversion of provider-side unavailability into user-facing states that implied exhausted allowance, insufficient plan or unavailable model. Those states direct different remedial actions and economic choices. Access-state integrity requires the system to distinguish account, entitlement, model and service availability so an infrastructure incident cannot masquerade as a reason to authenticate again, switch models or pay for a higher tier. The false allowance message supports the retained access-state failure. Its economic inducement materially engages Economic Solicitation Authenticity, but the source does not establish that AI-generated, AI-transformed or otherwise materially AI-mediated content produced or reinforced the misleading solicitation, independently of the product being an AI service. That recognition fact remains missing, so the economic role is corrected to ambiguous boundary with its prior failure preserved in the audit. No deceptive system intent, paid purchase or economic loss is inferred. Independent external assessment supports source-bounded repair in the restoration stage. The stakeholder communication-plan outcome remains Boundary because its complete planning evidence is unavailable. The SDOS governance-degradation candidate is excluded on its specific trigger or publication timing, rather than voluntary status.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident demonstrates that continuity, identity and economic controls need one coherent source of service state. Limit enforcement and upgrade prompts should be suppressed or explicitly qualified when provider telemetry indicates an outage; recovery messaging should identify which layer actually failed and avoid asking users to spend money or alter credentials for a provider-side condition.
